title: Closed immersions of algebraic spaces can be checked on a target atlas
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $a:E\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and choose a jointly surjective etale family $\{U_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ from schemes, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose for each $i$ the sheaf fibre product $E\times_YU_i$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] is represented by a scheme $Z_i$, and $Z_i\to U_i$ is a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $a$ is representable and every scheme base change $E\times_YT\to T$ is a closed immersion. No representability of $a$ is assumed in advance, and no finiteness or separation hypothesis is imposed on $E$, $Y$, or the family.

source.place: Tag 03M4 (lemma-closed-immersion-local), (4) implies (1), closed-immersion case; arbitrary family version by the scheme coproduct of the atlas.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary scheme $T$ and map $t:T\to Y$. Put $T_i=T\times_YU_i$. The fibre-product and covering lemma makes every $T_i$ a scheme and the family $\{T_i\to T\}$ jointly surjective etale. Etale scheme maps are flat and locally of finite presentation, so this is an fppf covering. On the big fppf site of $T$, define $F(W\xrightarrow{w}T)=\{e\in E(W):a(e)=t\circ w\}$. It is a sheaf: compatible local $e$ glue uniquely in the fppf sheaf $E$, and the equality with $t\circ w$ can be checked locally in the sheaf $Y$. This is the sheaf $E\times_YT$ viewed over $T$.

source.place: Tag 03M4 proof via spaces lemma-morphism-sheaves-with-P-effective-descent-etale: arbitrary scheme test and its pulled-back covering

proof.text: Set $W_i=Z_i\times_{U_i}T_i$. For every $T_i$-scheme $W$, a map $W\to W_i$ is precisely a map $W\to Z_i$ over $U_i$, hence an $E$-section whose image is the fixed map $W\to T_i\to U_i\to Y$. Thus $W_i$ represents $F|_{T_i}$, naturally in $W$. Its projection $c_i:W_i\to T_i$ is a closed immersion by scheme base change of $Z_i\to U_i$. The locally representable-sheaf/descent-data equivalence now supplies the scheme descent datum with these local representatives. Its overlap comparison retains the $E$-section and changes only the displayed base coordinates; on triple overlaps both composites retain exactly the same section and coordinates.

source.place: Tag 02W5 (lemma-descent-data-sheaves), with Tag 01QR for the local projections

proof.text: Each $c_i$ is separated by the closed-immersion permanence lemma. It is locally quasi-finite directly from the affine quotient description: over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T_i$ its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$; $R/J$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by the empty list. At a prime of $R/J$ with inverse image $\mathfrak p$ in $R$, one has $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and $(R/J)\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, by the mutually inverse maps $\bar r\otimes\lambda\mapsto r\lambda$ and $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$. The spectrum of this field has one point, which is isolated. This is exactly quasi-finiteness at that prime, hence local quasi-finiteness of $c_i$.

source.place: Tags 01QU (lemma-closed-immersion-separated), 01QO (affine quotient criterion), and lemma-immersion-locally-quasi-finite: its elementary closed-immersion case

proof.text: Apply effective fppf descent for separated locally quasi-finite scheme morphisms to the datum from step 2, using precisely the hypotheses verified in step 3. The datum is effective. The representability criterion in the locally representable-sheaf/descent-data equivalence therefore shows that $F$ is represented by a $T$-scheme $X_T$. In particular $X_T\times_TT_i\simeq W_i$ over $T_i$. This constructs representability of the scheme test; it has not been assumed.

source.place: lemma-morphism-sheaves-with-P-effective-descent-etale, using Tags 02W8 and 02W5 as in the proof of Tag 03M4

proof.text: The covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ is fpqc because it is fppf. The scheme morphism $X_T\to T$ becomes the closed immersion $W_i\to T_i$ after every member of this covering. Scheme-level fpqc descent of closed immersions gives that $X_T\to T$ is a closed immersion. This application is now between schemes, so it does not presuppose the representability being proved.

The scheme $T$ and map $T\to Y$ were arbitrary. Consequently every sheaf fibre product $E\times_YT$ is represented by the scheme $X_T$, and its projection is a closed immersion. By the definition of representable transformation this says that $a$ is representable and proves the claimed assertion for every scheme base change. All uses of descent allow arbitrary covering families and arbitrary base schemes, so no finiteness or separation condition on the atlas or the spaces was introduced.
